before_image.unique_thinking_zh: 罗瑞卿（1906-1978），四川南充人，中国人民解放军主要创建者之一，首任公安部部长、国防委员会副主席。他创造性地提出'安全立军思维'，将国家安全体系作为军队建设的核心基础，建立了从中央到地方的完整安全保卫制度。他倡导'整编革新思维'，在军队体制编制改革中大胆创新，推动军队正规化、现代化建设。罗瑞卿主张'参谋统筹思维'，善于从全局出发进行战略协调和资源调配。他强调'纪律严明法'，将铁的纪律作为军队战斗力的根本保证。他还提出'情报先行思维'，重视情报工作在国家安全中的关键作用。作为开国大将之一，他的安全保卫思想和军队整编实践为新中国国防安全体系奠定了坚实基础。
before_image.unique_thinking_en: Luo Ruiqing (1906-1978), from Nanchong, Sichuan, was one of the main founders of the Chinese People's Liberation Army and the first Minister of Public Security. He creatively proposed 'security-based military thinking,' making national security system the core foundation of military construction, establishing a complete security and defense system from central to local levels. He advocated 'reorganization and innovation thinking,' boldly innovating in military institutional reform, promoting the regularization and modernization of the military. Luo Ruiqing emphasized 'staff coordination thinking,' excelling in strategic coordination and resource allocation from a global perspective. He stressed 'iron discipline as law,' regarding strict discipline as the fundamental guarantee of military combat effectiveness. As one of the Ten Marshals, his security defense thoughts and military reorganization practice laid a solid foundation for New China's national defense security system.

after_image.unique_thinking_zh: 罗瑞卿（1906-1978），四川南充人，中国人民解放军的杰出领导人，新中国首任公安部部长（1949.10–1959.9），1955 年被授予大将军衔（开国十大大将之一）。主持公安工作期间，他确立「党委领导＋群众路线」的根本路线，形成「镇压与宽大相结合」的政策表述与「杀一批，关一批，管一批」的分类处置；在武装力量编成上主张军警分途，提出公安部队「既是公安，又是部队」、指挥关系属军委、工作关系属公安部；在纪律作风上以「不准坐霸王车、吃霸王饭、看霸王戏」立规并推动《公安人员八大纪律、十项注意》。他领导中央警卫工作，把「一要保证不出乱子，二要不脱离群众」的二元约束贯彻到部署细节；在军队政治工作中坚持政治与军事、政治与业务的辩证统一，反对「空头政治」；1978 年支持「实践是检验真理的唯一标准」的讨论，同年 8 月 3 日逝世，悼词与 1980 年平反通知为其官方评价坐标（相关条目均据 1949–1965 年文献与 1978/1980 年评价文件）。
after_image.unique_thinking_en: Luo Ruiqing (1906-1978), from Nanchong, Sichuan, was an outstanding leader of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army, the first Minister of Public Security of New China (Oct 1949 - Sep 1959), and one of the ten senior generals (1955). While leading public security work he established the fundamental line of Party committee leadership plus the mass line; he shaped the policy formulation of combining suppression with leniency and the classification of "execute a batch, imprison a batch, supervise a batch"; on the composition of armed forces he advocated separate tracks for police and military, holding that the public security forces are "both police and troops", with command belonging to the Military Commission and working relations to the Ministry of Public Security; on conduct he laid down the bans on "bully cars, bully meals and bully shows" and promoted the eight disciplines and ten attentions for public security personnel. He directed central guarding work and carried the dual constraint of "no disturbances and no divorce from the masses" into deployment detail; in military political work he upheld the dialectical unity of politics with military affairs and professional work, opposing "empty politics"; in 1978 he backed the debate on practice as the sole criterion of truth. He died on 3 August 1978; the eulogy and the 1980 rehabilitation notice form the coordinates of his official evaluation. (All entries are anchored to sources of 1949-1965 and the evaluative documents of 1978/1980.)
